title: The relative diagonal of an algebraic-space morphism is locally of finite type
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, with schemes [def-pc-scheme] and algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Let $g:U\to V$ be any morphism of algebraic spaces. Its diagonal $\Delta_g:U\to U\times_VU$ is representable and locally of finite type, where local finite type is tested on etale scheme charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Representable means that its pullback along every scheme mapping to $U\times_VU$ is a scheme. No finiteness or separation hypothesis is imposed on $g$, $U$, or $V$.

proof.text: Put $B=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ and $W=U\times_VU$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-diagonal-scheme-tests] to $g:U\to V$ over $B$. Its hypotheses are exactly that $B$ is a scheme and $U,V$ are algebraic spaces over $B$; it imposes no finiteness or separation conditions. For every scheme $T\to W$ it gives a scheme $D_T=U\times_WT$ with locally finite type projection $d_T:D_T\to T$. The existence of these schemes for all $T\to W$ is precisely representability of $\Delta_g$, as defined in [def-trf-algebraic-space].

source.place: Tag 03HK (lemma-properties-diagonal), (1)--(2), read with spaces.tex Tag 025V (definition-relative-representable-property); specialization of the existing scheme-test formulation.

proof.text: Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $T\to W$, which exists by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Step 1 says $D_T$ is a scheme and $d_T:D_T\to T$ is locally of finite type. In [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test] take $f=\Delta_g$, the target chart $T\to W$, and the source chart $D_T\to U\times_WT$ to be the identity. The identity is etale and surjective, so the criterion implies that $\Delta_g$ is locally of finite type in the etale-chart sense required here. This also handles the empty atlas when $W$ is empty.
